hints: Focus on what gas is made when an acid reacts with magnesium, and what s.t.p. tells you about converting volume to moles.
Work out moles of hydrogen first using 380 cm3 divided by 22400 cm3 mol-1, then remember two moles of a monocarboxylic acid make one mole of hydrogen.
Link mass to moles with Mr = mass divided by moles of acid to finish the calculation and pick the matching value.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of hydrogen gas**

Think of this as an acid plus metal reaction. The gas is hydrogen, $\text{H}_2$.

At s.t.p., 1 mol of any gas occupies $22400 \text{ cm}^3$:
$$\text{moles of H}_2 = \frac{380}{22400} = 0.01696 \text{ mol}$$

**Use the acid to hydrogen ratio**

A carboxylic acid with one $\text{-COOH}$ group is monoprotic. Two acid molecules give one $\text{H}_2$:
$$2\text{RCOOH} + \text{Mg} \rightarrow (\text{RCOO})_2\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2$$
So moles of acid Q is twice the moles of hydrogen:
$$\text{moles of Q} = 2 \times 0.01696 = 0.03393 \text{ mol}$$

**Calculate the relative formula mass**

Now connect the 4.00 g you started with to the moles you just found:
$$M_r = \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{moles}} = \frac{4.00}{0.03393} = 117.9$$
This rounds to 118, which matches one of the options.

options.A: 59 is exactly half the correct value. This happens if you use a 1:1 ratio of acid to hydrogen instead of 2:1, so you calculate moles of acid as 0.01696 mol. Always check the balanced equation for acids with metals.
options.B: 118 is correct. Moles of H2 is 0.01696 mol, so moles of monoprotic acid Q is 0.03393 mol, and Mr = 4.00 / 0.03393 = 118. This fits the 2RCOOH + Mg reaction.
options.C: 126 comes from using the wrong molar gas volume. If you divide by 24000 cm3 mol-1 (room temperature) instead of 22400 cm3 mol-1 (s.t.p.), you get Mr = 126. The question clearly states s.t.p.
options.D: 236 is double the correct value. This is the trap if you assume Q is a dicarboxylic acid with two -COOH groups, where 1 mol acid gives 1 mol H2. The question gives no evidence for two acid groups, so assume one -COOH group.
